strings.name: Paul McCartney
strings.summary: As a Beatles member, bassist and songwriter, Paul McCartney helped change popular song and recording practices with John Lennon and other collaborators. After the group ended, he continued solo work and formed Wings with Linda McCartney and Denny Laine. His work spans rock, pop and classical music, while decades of recording and performance connect different generations.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026; selected chronology extends to 2026-05-29. This is not a complete catalogue of works or appearances; later plans are not treated as completed events.
strings.influence.rationale: As a Beatle and solo songwriter, he has influenced popular-song structures, recording production and musical culture across generations.
strings.facts.fact-1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-2.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-2.value: Attended the Liverpool Institute boys’ grammar school
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Helping change popular song
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Combined melody, bass playing and studio experimentation in the Beatles’ collaborative writing and recording.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Creating beyond the band
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Developed different musical forms through solo albums, Wings and classical works.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Released The Boys of Dungeon Lane
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Worked with producer Andrew Watt on an album drawing substantially on memories of growing up.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Released McCartney III
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Created largely self-played and self-produced recordings during lockdown, continuing his self-titled series.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Received the Gershwin Prize
strings.timeline.event-3.text: The US Library of Congress honored his popular songwriting.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Received a knighthood
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Awarded a British knighthood for services to music.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Presented Liverpool Oratorio
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Collaborated with Carl Davis on an oratorio, extending his classical work.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Wings released Band on the Run
strings.timeline.event-6.text: The signature album consolidated a new phase after the Beatles.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Formed Wings
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Established a new group with Linda McCartney and Denny Laine.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Released his first solo album
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Issued McCartney as his work shifted toward a solo career around the Beatles’ breakup.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Helped create Sgt. Pepper’s
strings.timeline.event-9.text: With his Beatles colleagues, developed studio experimentation and album-wide concepts.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: The Beatles entered the record market
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Released Love Me Do before expanding internationally.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Met John Lennon
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Met at a Liverpool church event and later joined the Quarrymen.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Born in Liverpool
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Grew up in a musical family, learning instruments and writing songs as a teenager.
